claims.review_note:
Separate Hungarian-to-English language verification, 2026-09-24. Agent: /root/hungarian_language, started with fork_turns=none. Input contained only a neutral fidelity brief, the three original source URLs/sections and proposed English wording. The agent retrieved Hungarian source passages directly; no research record, prior conclusions, evidence statuses or PR discussions were supplied. This is a separate AI check, not independent human verification or legal interpretation. Initial comparison: 1. Decree 605/2022 section 1(1)(a): “Nemzeti Média- és Hírközlési Hatóság Hivatalát” = the Office of the National Media and Infocommunications Authority. Initial NMHH shorthand refined to Office of NMHH. 2. Decree section 1(3): “fizetési műveletek elfogadására vonatkozó pénzforgalmi szolgáltatás nyújtásához kapcsolódó fizetési terminálok” = payment terminals associated with providing a payment service concerning acceptance of payment transactions. Replaced vague “designated payment terminals” with payment terminals for payment-transaction acquiring services. 3. Act XVII section 1(2)(e): “az elektronikus könyvek és dedikált szoftverek” = electronic books and dedicated software. Added missing dedicated software to consumer-protection scope. 4. Decree section 1(1)(c),(e): transport class descriptions supported. Section 1(2), “integrált személyszállítási közszolgáltatás és összekapcsolt személyszállítási közszolgáltatás” = integrated passenger public service and interconnected passenger public service. Rail integrated/linked wording supported. Decree section 2 territorial detail is not required in the category list; this does not verify local office identities. 5. Decree section 1(1)(g), Act section 1(4): 112 emergency response supported as shorthand; refined to 112 emergency calls. 6. Annex 3(1): “az általános feltételekben vagy egy azzal egyenértékű dokumentumban” = in the general conditions or an equivalent document. Correction needed: “described in general terms” could suggest a nonspecific description; final wording explicitly says general terms and conditions. 7. Act section 6(1): “írásos és szóbeli formában” = in written and oral form; “nyilvánosságra kell hozni” = must be made public. Public-documentation summary supported. Documentation retention while service continues is part of source context, not a new table claim. 8. Act section 6(5): authority request covers compliance information and documentation; final wording includes both. 9. Act section 1(2)(c): “csak a ce) alpontot” = only subpoint ce). Urban/suburban/regional terminal-only wording supported as qualified shorthand; source excludes terminals integrated into vehicles, aircraft, ships and railway vehicles. 10. Act section 12(5): “2027. június 28-tól kell teljesíteni” = must be fulfilled from 28 June 2027. Specified 112-requirements wording supported, referring to section 1(4) and Annex 1 points 4.1.3 and 5. 11. MNB II.1: “azonosításra alkalmas tartalommal” = with content suitable for identification. Prior provider complaint must use published contacts and identify the complainant. Additional eligibility: no response, handling contrary to applicable rules, or suspected statutory consumer-right infringement apparent from the response. Proposed provider-first summary is supported because it explicitly retains linked eligibility conditions. 12. MNB II.1: “a szóbeli panaszról felvett jegyzőkönyvet” = the record drawn up of the oral complaint. Replaced broad “evidence of the original complaint” with the source's enumerated attachments: provider response, oral-complaint record, or proof of posting a postal complaint, as applicable. Postal destination explicitly supported; Hungary is an added country designation. Full identifying/content requirements remain in linked instructions. Final recheck by the same isolated language agent: Supported for all corrected passages and unchanged reviewed transport/transition shorthand. Corrected English grammar from “section 6(1) and Annex 3 requires” to “require” as requested. No material linguistic ambiguity remains in this reviewed wording. Authorities and statutory authority classes:

  • Office of NMHH – specified products, electronic communications and audiovisual-access services.
  • Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) – consumer banking, ATMs and payment terminals for payment-transaction acquiring services.
  • Consumer-protection authority – e-commerce, e-books and dedicated software, e-readers and payment terminals outside MNB's remit.
  • Civil aviation authority – covered air-passenger services and terminals.
  • Bus market-surveillance and passenger-rights authority – covered bus-passenger services and terminals.
  • Railway administrative body – covered rail services and terminals; integrated or linked public passenger services.
  • Maritime authority – covered water-passenger services and terminals.
  • Budapest Főváros Kormányhivatala – 112 emergency calls.
  • MNB, financial services: accessibility complaint instructions. After first complaining to the financial provider, complaints meeting the linked eligibility conditions may be posted to Magyar Nemzeti Bank, 1534 Budapest BKKP Pf. 777, Hungary. Attach the provider's response, the record of an oral complaint, or proof of posting a postal complaint, as applicable.
  • Other sectors: ❓ Unknown.

Act XVII of 2022, section 6(1) and Annex 3 require public accessibility documentation for covered services in accessible written and oral form, with compliance information in general terms and conditions or an equivalent document. Section 6(5) separately requires compliance information and documentation on the authority's request.

⚖️ EAA implementing law: Act XVII of 2022; implementing decree 605/2022.

Exact offices and websites for generic authority classes: Unknown. Urban, suburban and regional transport: covered terminal services only. Specified 112 requirements apply from 28 June 2027.
